title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices?

evidence_packet.title: What do Christmas market traders say about rising prices?
evidence_packet.lead: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
evidence_packet.summary: From £8 bratwursts to £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps, why is the cost of the markets rising year on year?
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mention Christmas markets these days and the conversation often turns to rising prices – from £8 bratwursts, £11 Yorkshire pudding wraps and even £5 for a few marshmallow sticks But what do the people behind the stalls think? Are they benefiting from the hikes or are their own profits being squeezed? Traders at Manchester's Christmas markets told the BBC they were feeling the pressure of increasing bills for staff, ingredients and energy, with some saying they were making less money despite charging more One trader said it costs at least £4,000 a day to run each her four stalls, while another has cut prices to keep customers coming back Nils Borstel, 25, helps run Bratwurst King, a family business which has operated at the markets since 1999 He said a sausage that previously cost £3.50 now sold for £8, with much of the increase taking place over the past five or six years

title: Conservative Party pays artist for Burnham images after legal threat

evidence_packet.title: Conservative Party pays artist for Burnham images after legal threat
evidence_packet.lead: Stanley Chow had threatened to sue the Conservative Party for using his illustrations of the PM
evidence_packet.summary: Stanley Chow had threatened to sue the Conservative Party for using his illustrations of the PM
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Conservatives have agreed to pay an artist who threatened to sue the party after it used his illustration of Andy Burnham to mock the prime minister Stanley Chow posted on Facebook that the party had used the picture - which Burnham has used on social media - without permission He had sought legal advice and threatened to take action against the party. It is understood the Tories agreed to pay a £1,000 fee for use of the image - and contributed an unknown sum to Chow's legal fees The Conservatives had distributed water bottles with the image on them - accusing Burnham of being a "bottler" Chow posted on Facebook: "The Conservative Party have settled after their recent indiscretion of using my image without my permission." He added: "Maybe ask first… admittedly I would have said no, but it would have been a damn sight cheaper for the Tory Party if they just hired any illustrator to do their take on a cartoon of Burnham… hopefully this a lesson learned. Copyright matters."

title: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen

evidence_packet.title: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen
evidence_packet.lead: Handmade wooden silhouettes of soldiers have been taken from a roundabout in Leigh
evidence_packet.summary: Handmade wooden silhouettes of soldiers have been taken from a roundabout in Leigh
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Dismay as Leigh veterans' handmade war memorial stolen - BBC News Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, The soldiers represent members of the armed forces who have died in conflicts since 1914 By Emma Jackson and Richard Stead , North West Published 13 November 2026 Veterans who handmade memorials to fallen soldiers were dismayed to find they had been stolen. They discovered that four of the wooden silhouettes had been taken from the display near Leigh Sports Village in in Greater Manchester was made earlier by members of a group set up to support ex-service people. George Brooks, who launched The Reeva Programme, said: "We are absolutely gutted. "I'm upset, I'm angry, and I'm sad, because I know the effort that went into making every single one of those crosses, making every single one of those tommies." Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, George Brooks founded The Reeva Programme CIC. The memorial, created on a roundabout, also features 1,228 white crosses to represent local members of the armed forces who were killed in World War Two and subsequent conflicts. George, 35, who served with the Army in Afghanistan, said the stolen figures were important to the community, and to thousands of people they were not just "pieces of wood". Image source, Reeva Programme Image caption, Reeva is named after a therapy dog that helped Brooks cope with PTSD after he left the Army The Reeva Programme provides fully trained assistance dogs to those who have served in the armed forces or emergency services. The theft has been reported to the police, but Brooks posted on social media to say that if whoever had stolen them were to return them, that would be the end of it. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Mayor of Greater Manchester has said the city region's combined authority is "preparing" for anti-social behaviour ahead of the roll-out of free bus travel for 11 to 16-year-olds From January, the current Our Pass scheme, which gives 16- 18-year-olds free travel on the Bee Network, will be extended to children from the age of 11 Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) confirmed that it was recruiting 20 extra travel safe and enforcement officers to support the 121 existing roles which coincided with the roll-out The city region's Mayor, Bev Craig said the combined authority had been working to make the Bee Network "even safer", and that "we trust our young people." Recent measures included the recent creation of the Transport Policing and Crime Command, which has seen 60 new police officers patrolling Manchester's trams and buses She said the new scheme for 11 to 16-year-olds, expected to benefit 200,000 young people, builds on the Our Pass scheme allowing free bus travel to those aged 16 to 18 which was rolled out in 2019

John Vickers triumphed in the Hindley Green by-election, held following the death of long-standing member Bob Brierley. He topped the polls with 1,201 votes and Reform's Bonnie Clarke was second with 887 votes. It marked the first Wigan borough election won by Labour this year, after they suffered a "wipe-out" in all 25 contested seats for the council in May's local elections. The Hindley Green ward is wholly in the Makerfield parliamentary constituency and the by-election was seen by many as a barometer of support for the new Prime Minister Andy Burnham, with polling happening in his own back yard. In May, Reform won 24 of the 25 seats contested. 'Disillusioned' Now, of the council's 75 seats, Labour have 43 councillors and overall control, Reform still have 25 members, and the remaining seven are independents. Reflecting on the rapid turn in his fortunes, Vickers acknowledged that Burnham's earlier win in Makerfield, on 18 June, "had a lot to do with tonight". He said: "People were disillusioned in May and what happened on June 18 certainly put a lot of faith back in people who had perhaps decided that the Labour Party was not going in the right direction." Outlining his priorities for the ward, he said: "The fact that Hindley Green has no NHS facilities is something we need to put right. title: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester

evidence_packet.title: Handmade gates craned into place at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester
evidence_packet.lead: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
evidence_packet.summary: The new gates at Rochdale Canal lock in Manchester replace ones installed more than 25 years ago
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network

title: Schools, libraries and parents face 'difficult decision' over David Walliams books

evidence_packet.title: Schools, libraries and parents face 'difficult decision' over David Walliams books
evidence_packet.lead: Some schools remove the children's author's books from their libraries after allegations against him
evidence_packet.summary: Some schools remove the children's author's books from their libraries after allegations against him
evidence_packet.evidence_text: "Head teachers are already making difficult decisions about whether or not these books should remain on the bookshelves of libraries at the moment," said Pepe Di'Iasio, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders "I'm aware from several of our members that they've already taken the decision to take them off their shelves." Walliams sold more than 50 million copies of books including Gangsta Granny and Billionaire Boy. He has denied allegations of sexual misconduct and abuses of power Darren Morgan, head of Kings Road Primary School in Manchester, told the programme that he has taken the decision to remove Walliams' publications The stories have been useful to promote reading, but "when there are these allegations it's really difficult to keep these books on the shelves", he said Steve Chalke, head of Oasis Academies, which runs more than 50 schools, said it was impossible to stop children seeing the current stories about Walliams

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Work has begun to restore lock gates across Greater Manchester's historical canal network A team has started fitting new handmade gates at Lock 80 on the Rochdale Canal, a waterway opened in 1804 as the first of three trans-Pennine canals, running between Manchester and Sowerby Bridge, West Yorkshire The new gates, at the lock to the east of the city centre in Manchester, were handcrafted from oak in Yorkshire, before being craned into place Each leaf of the upstream gate weighs one-and-a-half tonnes (1,500 kg), and the downstream leaves weigh two-and-a-half tonnes (2,500 kg). They replace gates that were installed at the turn of the millennium It comes after canal gates were replaced in the stretch of canal running through Manchester's Gay Village, in February The Canal and River Trust, the charity that cares for canals and waterways across England and Wales, said the work was one of hundreds of projects over the next five months set to maintain the 2,000-mile canal network

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A gold wristwatch thought to have belonged to Alan Turing has sold at auction for more than £75,000 The watch had been expected to fetch up to £10,000, but sold for a hammer price of £58,000, rising to £75,400 with fees Auctioneer Richard Bromell said a similar watch without the Turing connection would normally sell for about £300 to £400 "A lot of these things, they are bought with the heart, not necessarily the head," he said In 1976, the 9ct gold watch was given to a 15-year-old boy working at a hotel in Cheltenham by Joan Clarke, a fellow codebreaker and friend of Turing The boy was "perpetually late", prompting Clarke to gift him the watch to help him be on time. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham The battle in Oldham few knew was happening One person even said they preferred the paranormal over politics View 3 Images The Rochdale canal in Failsworth (Image: Copyright Unknown) Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 17:55, 13 Nov 2026 A tight contest has been fought in Oldham over the last month – but few people in the area knew it was even happening The Failsworth West by-election on November 12 saw poor turnout , with less than 20 per cent going to the polls and the number of votes cast totalling 1,547. This is less than half the number who turned out to vote earlier this year in the council ward Reform ended the night successfully defending the seat, with Coun Chris Baddeley joining Oldham council’s second largest political group. Labour saw an increase in support compared to May 2026 and doubling their vote share By-elections generally see lower turnout compared to wider elections and this week’s cold weather was thought to be a contributing factor. A sense of disillusionment with politics could have been one, too Out on the streets in and around Failsworth, many were unaware an election had just taken place. Some did not care with a jaded view of politicians, with one person even saying they preferred the paranormal over politics

After searching her symptoms online, she assumed the bleeding was caused by haemorrhoids But after experiencing a particularly heavy bleed, the mum of twins was referred by her GP for further tests Unfortunately, a colonoscopy revealed a large polyp. Subsequent biopsies and scans confirmed the devastating diagnosis of stage three recal cancer Charlotte said: "You just hear the word cancer, everything else goes blank. After searching her symptoms online, she assumed the bleeding was caused by haemorrhoids But after experiencing a particularly heavy bleed, the mum of twins was referred by her GP for further tests Unfortunately, a colonoscopy revealed a large polyp. Subsequent biopsies and scans confirmed the devastating diagnosis of stage three recal cancer Charlotte said: "You just hear the word cancer, everything else goes blank. From a distance, it looks as if he might be trying out a toy race car. But when the item started to They knew that this was a bid to smuggle contraband into the jail, a bid to undermine jail security. Within seconds of the drone making its way into the air, officers descened Nazar Al-Bakili, 35, who had moments earlier been operating the drone, threw away the controller and tried to run for it. evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS, police and fire services, along with schools, have warned people about emails being down and finding work-around ways to help keep in contact. evidence_packet.summary: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Saddleworth will have the opportunity to vote on the future of planning in their area when a referendum takes place on Thursday 10 December 2026. The referendum will ask residents whether they want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan to help decide planning applications in the area. The plan sets out local planning policies for Saddleworth and, if approved, will become part of the area’s statutory Development Plan, helping to guide decisions on future planning applications. Residents will be asked the following question: “Do you want Oldham Council and the Peak District National Park Authority to use the Neighbourhood Plan for Saddleworth to help it decide planning applications in the neighbourhood area?” To vote, residents must be registered to vote in local government elections and have a qualifying address within the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Area. The deadline to register to vote is Tuesday 24 November 2026. Residents who wish to vote by post, proxy or who need a Voter Authority Certificate should also be aware of the following deadlines: - Wednesday 25 November, 5pm: Deadline for new postal vote applications and changes to existing postal voting arrangements. - Wednesday 2 December, 5pm: Deadline for new proxy vote applications and applications for a free Voter Authority Certificate. - Thursday 10 December, 5pm: Deadline for emergency proxy vote applications, where eligible. Residents can read the Saddleworth Neighbourhood Plan and supporting referendum documents online at: https://www.oldham.gov.uk/info/201235/neighbourhood_planning/2936/saddleworth_neighbourhood_plan Paper copies are also available to view at Lees, Uppermill, Delph and Greenfield libraries, Oldham Council’s reception

Councillors represent the Council to the community and the community to the Council. Anyone wishing to stand for election can obtain a nomination pack from the Elections Office at the J.R.Clynes Building, Cultural Quarter, Greaves Street, Oldham, OL1 1AL, between 9am and 5pm, or they can be emailed on request by emailing election@oldham.gov.uk. Royton Hall Primary School, St Martin’s Primary School and Greenfield Primary School were recognised as the schools with the highest participation out of 92 schools taking part across Oldham. Representatives from Oldham Libraries and partner Kajima, which supports opportunities to encourage children to read and celebrate their success, visited each school to award book tokens in recognition of pupils’ commitment to reading. Kajima have sponsored the Summer Reading Challenge for the sixth year running, encouraging Oldham children towards a lifelong love of books. The challenge highlights the importance of partnerships between schools, libraries and local organisations in supporting children’s literacy, building reading confidence and making reading an exciting and rewarding experience. evidence_packet.lead: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances
evidence_packet.summary: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Get ready for a spooky spectacle packed with jaw-dropping performances. Prepare to be wowed in town this Saturday, with an evening packed with entertainment from 5.30pm to 7.30pm. The free event, as part of Oldham's year as the Greater Manchester Town of Culture, will transform Parliament Square into a spook-tacular Halloween and Bonfire Night-inspired celebration with jaw-dropping fiery performances and roaming characters. Visitors can experience the thrills of Juggling Inferno, the spectacular fire and pyrotechnic displays of Helter Skelter Arts, and The Lips Halloween Show. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Sun 15th Nov, 2026 - Locations across Stockport town centre ©Matthew Nichol Photography Stockport’s Spectacular Sunday Locations across Stockport town centre Sun 15th Nov, 2026 12pm - 5pm Go to Manchester's Finest X profile A giant snow lion, a circus adventure into space and the world’s smallest nightclub. Stockport is kicking off Christmas in suitably weird and wonderful fashion, as Spectacular Sunday returns for its fourth year on Sunday 15 November More than 200 performers and 50 free shows will take over the town centre, transforming streets and squares into stages for giant puppets, circus acts, live music, comedy and all manner of festive surprises Among the highlights is the enormous Snow Lion, joined by dancing elves and towering stiltwalkers. There’s also Over The Moon, a circus adventure with an intergalactic twist, and Hydropunk, an interactive spectacle involving water-powered pipes, pumps, sprays and puzzles And if you fancy a rave between the Christmas shopping, The Miniscule of Sound, officially the world’s smallest nightclub, is back for another year. evidence_texts: Credit: Gus Gregory Co-op Live Etihad Campus, 1 Sportcity Way, Manchester M11 3DL 14 November 2026 Paul Heaton brings his huge UK arena tour to Co-op Live this month, celebrating more than 40 years of unforgettable songwriting. Ahead of their massive Heaton Park take over next summer, the Dublin boys are set to give fans a first listen to their spectacular new album ‘ Dopamine Chamber ‘ live on stage. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wednesday 12 May 2027 – Band on the Wall Thursday 13 May 2027 – Southbank Centre Sona Jobarteh is the first professional female kora virtuoso to emerge from any of West Africa’s five Griot dynasties, and a singer, composer and bandleader whose concerts fill some of the world’s finest halls. In 2026 she sold out the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg, played Munich’s Prinzregententheater and the Schleswig-Holstein Musik Festival, and on October 11 received the Silicon Valley African Film Festival’s 2026 Icon Award for her contributions to African music, scholarship and cultural promotion. On stage, Sona sings and plays the 21-string kora and guitar, joined by Eric Appapoulay, also on guitar, Andi McLean on bass, Yuval Wetzler on drums, Anselmo Neto on percussion and her son, Sidiki Jobarteh, on balafon. The show blends Mandé griot tradition with blues, Afropop and contemporary songwriting. She has also toured with blues legend Taj Mahal. Her concerts have become events wherever she plays. She has performed more than a hundred shows across Europe, Africa, the United States and beyond, in some of the world’s most prestigious theaters and festivals, with sell-outs at London’s Barbican, Cologne’s Philharmonie and the Seine Musicale in Paris, and appearances at the Hollywood Bowl, Symphony Space in New York and WOMAD Australia and New Zealand. Her latest album, Badinyaa Kumoo, was named one of the best albums of its year by Songlines Magazine, and her single “Gambia” has passed 32 million YouTube views. Recent collaborations include a feature on LL Cool J’s album The FORCE, on the song “Black Code Suite”, and a guest appearance on “Se a Vida Pede” from the Brazilian group Gilsons’ latest album. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been part of Manchester since 1867. A £300,000 restoration, long-term lease and 23-year-old head chef are shaping what comes next Go to Manchester's Finest X profile Mr Thomas’s Chop House has been serving Manchester since 1867, but owner Roger Ward admits there was a point after Covid when he wasn’t sure how much longer he wanted to keep doing it Tom’s had gone eight years without a proper lease and much longer without any meaningful investment by the landlord. Retirement was being seriously considered. Instead, Roger decided to “go again properly” That decision has resulted in a new long-term commitment to the Chop Houses and around £300,000 being spent restoring Tom’s – touching everything from the dining rooms and furniture to the menu, wine list, kitchen and beer cellars Roger is particularly pleased with the toilets “Tom’s was famous for the shittest toilets in town,” he says. They are now, by his assessment, considerably less so. Downstairs has been redone, upstairs has new ones too, while a previously overlooked back room has been completely reworked

It is Open Restaurant Group’s ninth restaurant to date and its second site in Greater Manchester, following the launch of Arcadian in Didsbury in Sep At the focus of the restaurant is a four-to-five-seat chef’s counter, which places guests directly at the pass for an up-close view of the kitchen in action. The interiors feature four-metre elm trees, curved booth seating and a brass wine display, so the atmosphere and experienc Award-winning Andrew Sheridan brings his internationally inspired approach to Counter, building on a career that has seen multiple restaurants under his direction feature in the prestigious Michelin Guide. At Counter, he challenges convention by exploring what British cooking can The menu puts this philosophy into practice with dishes that combine unexpected ingredients and inventive flavour pairings. Highlights include the Beef Tartare Pressed Croissant, pairing aged beef with a crispy pressed croissant, smoked oyster mayo, wasabi and pickled shallot and From the grill, guests can enjoy the Satay Spatchcock Chicken, served with peanut satay, fermented chilli, coconut, burnt lime and crispy shallot, alongside the slow-cooked Thai Lamb Shoulder, served with red thai sauce, chilli and coriander

evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.evidence_text: L-R: Simon Shaw, Anna Dick, Alastair Brown, Tripti Anil, Alan Jackson Simon Shaw, Delivery Director at Codurance, hosted the lunchtime session for tech leaders and introduced Codurance, which is a global software engineering consultancy that has run its Manchester office for 15 years He was joined on the panel by Anna Dick, Chief Technology & Product Officer at Capsule; Alastair Brown, Group Director of AI and Technology at Peninsula; Tripti Anil, Senior Leader, Data & Analytics at Kellanova; and Alan Jackson, Director of Client Solutions at Codurance Talking about discovering how AI can be used in projects, Anna said that Capsule's initial three months of AI exploration across all its business teams built appetite for further experimentation, but it also got a little out of control. At Peninsula, one initiative focused on giving customers richer answers and delivered over £1m in revenue. He said success depends on strong sponsorship and expertise from wi Tripti described spending three years building data foundations at Kellanova, focusing on "the right things at the right time" and bringing business teams along on the journey. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this month Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Coinciding with the homecoming show at Albert Hall, The Durutti Column have joined with Four Tet for an official remix of Your Shadow at Morning. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Credit: ChrisJamesRyanPhotography Co-op Live Etihad Campus, 1 Sportcity Way, Manchester M11 3DL 19 November 2026 Following a legendary tiny gig at Manchester’s Satan’s Hollow in the spring, Enter Shikari make a welcome return to the city this November. Upgrading somewhat to the biggest arena in Manchester, the band are set to pack out Co-op Live with some of their greatest hits and plenty of new material. Since forming in 2003 at school in their hometown of St Albans, Enter Shikari have so far released seven full-length studio albums , and this tour will likely celebrate all of them – with 2023’s ‘ A Kiss for the Whole World ‘ being the latest. Expect a stunning performance and out-of-this-world atmosphere as Enter Shikari play their biggest Manchester show yet. Read more

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Credit: Rachel/Murray Stringer The Warehouse Aviva Studios, Water St, Manchester M3 4JQ Nov 23, 24 Bloc Party and Interpol head to Manchester for a co-headline tour , taking over the Warehouse space at Aviva Studios. title: Old Trafford's 'once-in-a-generation' plan that could be ruined by 'weeing in the garden'

evidence_packet.title: Old Trafford's 'once-in-a-generation' plan that could be ruined by 'weeing in the garden'
evidence_packet.lead: Residents want to see a solution to matchday parking problems, related anti-social behaviour and the use of alleys and front gardens as an alternative to actual toilets
evidence_packet.summary: Residents want to see a solution to matchday parking problems, related anti-social behaviour and the use of alleys and front gardens as an alternative to actual toilets
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester United FC Old Trafford's 'once-in-a-generation' plan that could be ruined by 'weeing in the garden' Residents want to see a solution to matchday parking problems, related anti-social behaviour and the use of alleys and front gardens as an a A ‘once-in-a-generation' regeneration opportunity is being brought forward in Old Trafford - but it risks being overshadowed by matchday anti-social behaviour, neighbours fear Trafford council , the Greater Manchester Combined Authority and Manchester United FC are teaming up on an ambitious project that could see a forgotten part of the borough transformed beyond recognition. Bosses want to see ‘thriving’ new communities built in the Wharfside area, w Commercial spaces, eateries, hotels and offices are also in the line-up . And at the heart of the development – and the catalyst for it – is a proposed new stadium to replace the Theatre of Dreams With 100,000 seats, Man U’s promised new home ground is expected to be the largest in the UK. The Wharfside scheme is likely to take decades to deliver in full But the results of a consultation on a plan suggest that, for some residents in the area, their priorities are more immediate and their ambitions for the area somewhat less lofty
